correctness.rationale: Gaussian regression gives the conditional fourth-moment polynomial exactly, valid also for singular covariance. Gamma-function recurrence yields normalized second and fourth weighted Gaussian moments (1-s) and (1-s)(3-s), which reduce the signed blockwise difference to -s[a²+b²+4abc-(2+s)a²b²]. The three-by-three PSD constraint bounds the transformed correlation w from below by uv-sqrt((1-u²)(1-v²)). Substitution, u²+v²>=2uv, and sqrt((1-u²)(1-v²))<=1-uv yield F>=-2q+(6-s)q²>=-1/(6-s) globally. Equality requires q=1/(6-s), equal incident magnitudes, and the singular lower correlation boundary, giving precisely the stated rank-two matrices. Positive-definite approximation proves sharpness in the nonsingular class. Both the exact sign criterion and the complete equality classification are thus proved for all 0<s<1.

originality.rationale: The directly motivating Russell–Sun 2022 full text treats one negative and one positive power only. Zhou et al. 2023 provide non-sharp multivariate mixed-sign lower and upper comparison bounds, not the exact joint-positive-block sign criterion or the optimal additive deviation. The later Lan–Ouimet–Sun convex-order upper bound does not cover the nonconvex function x2²x3². Known multivariate bounds for the raw mixed moment cannot fix the sign or sharp magnitude of the group-centered difference because the positive-block comparator depends quadratically on the free correlation. Exact formula, parameter, general broader theorem, and database searches found no covering result. The residual risk of implicit prior elementary elliptope optimization is noted.
residual_risks: An equivalent group-centered correlation-elliptope optimization could be implicit in older Gaussian regression or moment-inequality work under different terminology.
The proposed finding uses a blockwise rather than fully factorized benchmark; equivalent blockwise inequalities under older terminology might be difficult to locate.

value.rationale: The bivariate opposite Gaussian product inequality does not describe the effect of replacing one positive-power coordinate by a dependent quadratic pair. The first three-coordinate case has a natural groupwise comparison, and the theorem supplies its complete sign phase diagram, the globally optimal maximum violation s/(6-s), the unique rank-two extremal geometry up to signs, and explicit exact counterexamples. This is a meaningful structural boundary for extending opposite product principles to nonconvex positive blocks, not a numerical parameter slice or a mere normalization check.
